claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The ductile-brittle-ductile transition in high-entropy alloys is caused by their compositional complexity and microstructural characteristics.
High-entropy alloys have diverse elemental compositions.
A temperature range that induces temper embrittlement in conventional alloys can be used to test high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys possess a complex microstructure and phase distribution.
Interactions among multiple elements in high-entropy alloys prevent the formation of embrittling phases.
The embrittling phases allegedly prevented in high-entropy alloys are common in conventional alloys.
High-entropy alloys will display a ductile-brittle-ductile transition as temperature varies.
At certain temperatures, high-entropy alloys may have greater ductility than conventional alloys.
The proposed behavior is limited to high-entropy alloys rather than all alloy systems.
The exact temperature range of the proposed transition is unknown.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says compositional complexity prevents embrittling phases, but the predicted outcome includes an intermediate brittle regime. No alternative cause of that brittle regime is supplied, so the mechanism does not coherently explain the full ductile-brittle-ductile transition.

The relevant transition temperature range is left unspecified, yet absence of a transition within an arbitrarily tested range is declared falsifying. Without a predefined range, a negative result is not necessarily decisive.
